title: Submission fees and tip jars: when it’s worth paying to submit
seoTitle: Literary Magazine Submission Fees and Tip Jars: When to Pay
description: Why some literary magazines charge reading fees, when a contest fee is fair, what an optional tip jar really is, and how to find magazines that read for free.
summary: Reading fees, contest fees and tip jars: what each one buys, when to pay, and how to find magazines that read for free.
answer: A submission fee pays for your work to be read, not accepted. An optional tip jar should let you submit without paying. Pay only when the magazine fits your work, the terms are clear and the fee fits your budget. Free reading periods, fee waivers and no-fee magazines keep regular submitting affordable.
keyPoints: A reading fee pays for consideration. It doesn’t buy a better chance of acceptance.
A tip jar is only optional if the same submission goes through without paying.
Set a yearly limit you can afford without an acceptance, and log every fee.
illustrationAlt: Illustration separating a required reading fee from an optional donation.
